title: Process Design and Economics
description: This syllabus is designed for a senior chemical engineering course that bridges core ChE science with plant-scale design decisions. Students should leave able to synthesize a flowsheet, size major equipment, simulate and validate a design, estimate capital and operating costs, evaluate profitability, and defend safety, environmental, and economic recommendations.

topics.title: Process Synthesis and Flowsheet Development
topics.description: Introduces the creative core of process design: turning chemistry, separations, recycle structures, utilities, and constraints into a coherent plant flowsheet.

children.title: Design basis and process objectives
children.description: Students learn to define the production target, feed assumptions, product specifications, and design boundaries before calculating anything.

children.title: Reaction-separation-recycle structure
children.description: Flowsheet synthesis connects reactors, separation trains, recycle loops, purge streams, and heat recovery into a workable system.

children.title: Process flow diagrams
children.description: PFDs communicate the material and energy logic of the plant and become the backbone for simulation and costing.

topics.title: Material and Energy Balances for Design
topics.description: Makes sure students can close the balances that every design decision depends on, especially around recycle, purge, conversion, yields, and energy integration.

children.title: Steady-state process balances
children.description: Mass and energy balances are used to size streams, estimate duties, and detect impossible designs.

children.title: Recycle and purge calculations
children.description: Recycle structures improve yield and economics but require careful handling of accumulation and inert buildup.

children.title: Utility and heat-duty estimation
children.description: Energy requirements are translated into steam, cooling water, refrigeration, fuel, and electrical utility needs.

topics.title: Equipment Sizing and Selection
topics.description: Turns the flowsheet into physical equipment with preliminary sizes, operating ranges, materials, and constraints suitable for cost estimation and design review.

children.title: Major equipment sizing
children.description: Students estimate sizes for reactors, vessels, heat exchangers, pumps, compressors, and separation units at a scoping level.

children.title: Equipment selection tradeoffs
children.description: Selection is framed as a balance among performance, cost, reliability, controllability, safety, and maintainability.

children.title: Design margins and practical constraints
children.description: Students learn why real equipment includes margins, vendor ranges, pressure drops, fouling factors, and constructability limits.

topics.title: Process Simulation Software
topics.description: Develops practical fluency in simulation tools while emphasizing that software output must be checked against engineering judgment and independent calculations.

children.title: Property methods and component data
children.description: Students learn that thermodynamic models determine whether simulation results are meaningful for real mixtures.

children.title: Flowsheet modeling workflow
children.description: Simulation becomes a systematic process of specifying units, convergence blocks, recycles, and design specs.

children.title: Model validation and sanity checks
children.description: Students compare simulation results with hand calculations, literature values, and physical expectations.

topics.title: Capital Cost Estimation
topics.description: Shows how preliminary equipment sizes become installed capital estimates, with explicit attention to uncertainty and estimate class.

children.title: Purchased equipment cost
children.description: Students estimate base equipment cost from size, capacity, pressure, material, and scaling correlations.

children.title: Installed and indirect costs
children.description: Total capital includes installation, piping, instrumentation, electrical, buildings, engineering, contingency, and working capital.

children.title: Estimate accuracy and uncertainty
children.description: Cost numbers are interpreted as decision-support estimates rather than exact predictions.

topics.title: Operating Cost Estimation
topics.description: Builds the annual cost model that links raw materials, utilities, labor, maintenance, waste treatment, and overhead to plant profitability.

children.title: Variable costs
children.description: Variable costs scale with production and often dominate chemical-process economics.

children.title: Fixed and semi-fixed costs
children.description: Fixed costs keep the plant running regardless of throughput and shape break-even behavior.

children.title: Cost of manufacturing
children.description: Students combine cost categories into a clear cost-of-goods or cost-of-manufacturing model.

topics.title: Profitability Analysis and Project Evaluation
topics.description: Translates process performance into business decisions using discounted cash flow and project evaluation metrics.

children.title: Cash-flow construction
children.description: Students build project cash flows from capital spending, revenue, operating costs, taxes, depreciation, and working capital.

children.title: Economic metrics
children.description: Decision metrics compare alternatives across time and risk using consistent financial assumptions.

children.title: After-tax and inflation effects
children.description: More realistic analysis includes tax treatment, depreciation schedules, escalation, and real versus nominal assumptions.

topics.title: Decision Analysis, Sensitivity, and Risk
topics.description: Gives students tools to make defensible recommendations when prices, yields, capital costs, demand, and technical performance are uncertain.

children.title: Sensitivity analysis
children.description: Students identify which assumptions drive project value and where better data would matter most.

children.title: Decision trees and expected value
children.description: Decision analysis frames staged projects, uncertain outcomes, and information-gathering choices.

children.title: Multi-criteria tradeoffs
children.description: Not every design decision is purely financial; students compare safety, emissions, operability, schedule, and strategic fit.

topics.title: Process Optimization
topics.description: Shows how engineers improve a process by choosing decision variables, constraints, and objective functions tied to cost, profit, energy, yield, or emissions.

children.title: Objective functions and constraints
children.description: Optimization begins by clearly stating what is being improved and what physical, economic, and safety limits must hold.

children.title: Design-variable selection
children.description: Students learn to identify variables that are controllable and meaningful at design stage.

children.title: Optimization with simulation
children.description: Simulation-based optimization is treated as an iterative engineering workflow, not a black-box answer machine.

topics.title: Safety and HAZOP Analysis
topics.description: Places process safety at the center of design, using structured hazard identification and inherently safer thinking before finalizing equipment and economics.

children.title: Hazard identification
children.description: Students learn to recognize chemical, thermal, pressure, toxicity, flammability, and reactivity hazards in a flowsheet.

children.title: HAZOP method
children.description: HAZOP provides a structured team method for finding deviations, causes, consequences, safeguards, and recommendations.

children.title: Relief and inherently safer design
children.description: Safety is improved by eliminating hazards where possible and protecting against credible overpressure or loss-of-control events.

topics.title: Environmental and Sustainability Considerations
topics.description: Expands process design beyond economics to emissions, waste, water, energy intensity, lifecycle effects, and regulatory expectations.

children.title: Environmental releases and waste
children.description: Students estimate and reduce air, water, and solid-waste impacts from process alternatives.

children.title: Energy efficiency and integration
children.description: Energy use is treated as both an operating-cost issue and an environmental performance driver.

children.title: Sustainability metrics
children.description: Students evaluate designs with broader metrics that can influence process selection and stakeholder acceptance.

topics.title: Design Case Studies and Alternative Evaluation
topics.description: Uses realistic cases to integrate flowsheet synthesis, sizing, simulation, economics, safety, environment, and uncertainty into complete design choices.

children.title: Case-study framing
children.description: Students practice translating an open-ended industrial problem into assumptions, alternatives, and evaluation criteria.

children.title: Alternative comparison
children.description: Design alternatives are compared using consistent technical and economic assumptions.

children.title: Lessons learned
children.description: Case review helps students see how design decisions interact and how early assumptions can dominate later results.

topics.title: Design Report, Presentation, and Professional Review
topics.description: Makes the course deliverable-ready by teaching students to communicate assumptions, calculations, risks, economics, and recommendations in professional design-review formats.

children.title: Technical design report
children.description: Students learn to document a design so another engineer can audit the basis, calculations, and recommendation.

children.title: Economic recommendation
children.description: The final economic argument must connect technical performance, uncertainty, and decision criteria.

children.title: Oral design defense
children.description: Presentation practice prepares students to answer questions from technical, safety, business, and management audiences.
